extracted.intended_audience: military legal officers, judge advocates, convening authorities, and commanders responsible for courts-martial
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing the convening, composition, duties, and conduct of courts-martial and the role and responsibilities of judge advocates and convening authorities in military trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening authority determination of member seniority
rubrics_metrics.description: Held that the convening authority is the sole judge of whether or not it is possible to constitute a court of members all superior in rank to the accused, and that his decision as indicated by the convening order is conclusive upon the court as to that matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical officers' eligibility for detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Either a Medical Reserve Corps officer when lawfully on active duty, or a dental surgeon commissioned as such, is legally eligible for detail as a member of a general court-martial or as a trial officer of a summary court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, because the sick may at any time require the attention of a doctor, a medical officer should not be detailed to court-martial duty when it can be avoided. See R. 22, 536, Dec., 1866; 23, 522, June, 1867; C. 13150, Aug. 19, 1902; etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any commissioned officer may be appointed judge advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: Any commissioned officer may legally be appointed judge advocate of a court-martial (e.g., a surgeon, assistant surgeon, or a chaplain is legally eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian judge advocates employment is rare and restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: While a civilian may legally be appointed or employed as judge advocate of a court-martial, such employment has been of the rarest occurrence in the military service and is more frequent in naval than military courts-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After transfer of authority to employ counsel to the Department of Justice (act of June 22, 1870), neither the Secretary of War nor the Secretary of the Navy is authorized to retain a civilian lawyer to act as judge advocate. See 13 Op. Atty. Gen. 514; 14 id. 13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate conflict of interest prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer cannot, in general, fitly or becomingly act as judge advocate in a case in which he is personally interested as accuser or prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the judge advocate prepared the charges and was the accuser and entertained strong personal prejudice, he is unfit to act, especially as prosecuting official and adviser to the court. R. 41, 413, Dec., 1885. Signing charges without personal prejudice may not improperly disqualify him. P. 63, 240, Jan., 1894.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desirability of judge advocate neutrality
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable to detail as judge advocate, if practicable, an officer who has no considerable prejudice against the party to be tried, or any decided personal interest in his case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection of an officer who is a material witness or stands to be promoted if accused is dismissed is an unfortunate selection. R. 21, 177, Jan., 1866; 31, 361, May, 1871.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief of judge advocate pending trial but not after for authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: While a judge advocate may be relieved pending a trial and a new one appointed, it would not be proper to make such a change after the conclusion of a trial simply for the purpose of having the record authenticated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondelegable appointment of court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of a court-martial cannot be legally delegated to a staff officer as a routine duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court independence and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial is to be left independent as to matters within its own discretion, but may not assume authority over subjects belonging to the province of the convening officer; it cannot properly refuse to proceed on grounds such as inadequate punishment power, presence of junior officers on the detail, or that the accused has not been placed in arrest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a court improperly declines, the convening authority may peremptorily order it to proceed; if refusal continues, preferable course is dissolution in general orders and convening a new court. R. 21, 177, Jan., 1866; 25, 578, May, 1868; 28, 57, Aug., 1868.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice of examining multiple accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is established practice before courts-martial and military commissions to examine into as many accusations against the individual on trial, without regard to connection of date/place, as the prosecuting authority deems proper; charges may be unlimited in number and character within tribunal jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should, if practicable, be consolidated and one trial had upon the whole. R. 14, 40, Jan., 1865; R. 30, 265, Apr., 1870.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander restoring deserter cannot impose punishment conditionally
rubrics_metrics.description: A commander, in restoring a deserter to duty without trial according to the Army Regulations, is not authorized to require him to submit to a punishment as a condition to his being so restored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bringing charges before general court-martial when dishonorable discharge possible
rubrics_metrics.description: If punishment may be dishonorable discharge because of previous convictions, the department commander may properly require the charges to be brought to trial before a general court-martial notwithstanding that the alternative punishment (if not dishonorable discharge) would be within power of an inferior court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening authority's duty to consider prosecution interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The convening authority should consider each case carefully and be satisfied that its prosecution is for the best interests of the Government before he refers charges to a court; no prescribed form of consideration is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He may refer charges to inspector general or other officer but is not required to do so. C. 19854, June 29, 1906.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of simultaneous trials for related offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier may legally be tried at the same time for fraudulent enlistment and for desertion therefrom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct offenses tried by appropriate tribunal
rubrics_metrics.description: Desertion and joining the enemy/taking service with enemy are distinct offenses; desertion ordinarily tried by a general court-martial as violation of Articles of War, while joining the enemy would be tried by a military commission as a violation of the laws of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comity of civil and military jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: As a principle of comity between civil and military tribunals, the jurisdiction which first attaches in a particular case should be carried to its termination; a request of civil authorities for surrender of the prisoner may be denied if military jurisdiction has already attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil conservator does not remove military jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer could not, by consenting to being placed under a 'conservator' as a habitual drunkard in form prescribed by local law, withdraw himself from military jurisdiction; he remained amenable to trial and punishment for offenses committed prior to such proceeding and within limitation period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral qualification cases should be tried by court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: Where administrative examination raises questions as to moral qualifications, such cases should be tried by court-martial—the agency provided by law for investigation and punishment of offenses in violation of Articles of War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nolle prosequi authority reserved to Government, not judge advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: A prosecution before a court-martial proceeds in the name of the Government; the Secretary of War or convening military commander may require or authorize the judge advocate to enter a nolle prosequi, but the judge advocate cannot exercise this authority at his own discretion, nor can the court direct it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for explanation prior to bringing charges
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where charges are apparently susceptible of reasonable explanation, it is not unusual—especially where charges are preferred by an inferior against a superior—to afford the officer charged an opportunity to make explanation before determining whether to bring him to trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications protocol between convening authority and court
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from the convening authority to the court (and vice versa) should be made to/by the president as its organ, unless the court directs the judge advocate to represent it; communications relating to the conduct of the prosecution should be made to/by the judge advocate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening order authentication and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: An order convening a general court-martial should properly be headed and authenticated so as to show it was issued by an officer authorized by statute law (Articles of War) to create such a tribunal; an order signed by an officer describing himself merely as commanding a 'post' or 'district' is prima facie invalid though capable of validation by proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate judge-advocate for each general court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate judge-advocate should be appointed for each general court-martial convened; the same officer may be selected repeatedly but should be detailed anew for every court on which he acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment in a general order of a particular officer to act as judge advocate for all courts to be held in the same command is irregular. R. 2, 54, Mar., 1863; 16, 429, Aug., 1865.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate may not entertain charges in first instance
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate is not authorized to entertain charges in the first instance; he may properly act—serve charges, prepare case for trial—only when charges are transmitted to him for that purpose by the convening officer or the officer who detailed him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate should not materially modify transmitted charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Where charges already formally preferred are transmitted to the judge advocate for prosecution, he should not assume to modify them in material particulars without authority from the convening officer; he may correct obvious mistakes of form or slight errors in names, dates, amounts, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: He cannot make substantial amendments, reject or withdraw a charge or enter a nolle prosequi, or substitute a new and distinct charge without authority. R. 2, 60, Mar., 1863; 21, 56, Nov., 1865; P. 20, 378, Nov., 1887.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to appoint reporter vested in judge advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: The power to appoint the reporter (section 1203, R.S.) is vested exclusively in the trial judge advocate and cannot be exercised by the court; employment of a stenographic reporter should be resorted to only in an important case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of enlisted men as reporters and pay limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: By circular (1898) employment of enlisted men as reporters authorized 'without extra expense to the United States.' Under regulations no person in military or civil service can lawfully receive extra compensation for clerical duties performed for a military court; in war time no additional increased compensation allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that no extra pay can be allowed an enlisted man for services as reporter. C. 5434, Dec., 1898; 7334, Nov., 1899.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate subpoena power limited to court testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate is authorized to subpoena witnesses only for testifying in court; he cannot summon a witness to appear before himself for preliminary examination—he must procure an order issued by the proper commander for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when forwarding interrogatories for deposition
rubrics_metrics.description: When forwarding interrogatories for a deposition the judge advocate should transmit with them a subpoena (in duplicate) requiring the witness to appear at a stated place and date before the person to take the deposition; particulars not ascertained may be left blank to be supplied by the officer serving the subpoena; when deposition returned transmit certificate of attendance and copy of the convening order, duration ascertained from deposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on employing civil officials to serve subpoenas if compensation arises
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate has no authority to employ a civil official or private civilian to serve subpoenas if by so doing the United States will be subjected to a claim for compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of necessary expenses to locate witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate may certify as necessary for 'Expenses of courts-martial' the necessary expense incident to locating a material witness who had been duly summoned before the court and who had disobeyed the summons and left his former place of abode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of expert for insanity defense with approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If in the trial of an officer the accused raises insanity as a defense, the judge advocate may, with the approval of superior authority, employ on behalf of the Government an expert in mental diseases with a view to placing him on the stand as a witness; the necessary expense is a proper charge against the appropriation for expenses of courts-martial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only judge advocates may issue process to compel attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1202, R.S., authorizes only judge advocates of courts-martial to issue process to compel the attendance of witnesses; the court itself (general or inferior) has no such power; the judge advocate is authorized only to initiate the process of attachment—the statute does not specify by whom it shall be executed and he cannot command any officer or person to serve it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment and brief detention of civilian witness may be warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate who attached a civilian witness brought to the place of the court and detained him one hour in the guardhouse before bringing him before the court was held to be warranted under section 1202, R.S., and prosecution for false imprisonment was to be discontinued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate cannot arrest accused or compel attendance by force
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate has no authority to place in arrest an officer or soldier about to be tried by the court, or to compel attendance of the accused by requiring a noncommissioned officer to bring him; these duties devolve upon the convening authority or post commander or other proper officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate should normally not give unsolicited legal opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is proper practice for a judge advocate not to give his opinion upon a point of law arising upon a military trial unless required by the court, though opinions suitably tendered are generally received; if the court objects he is not authorized to attempt to give it or enter it upon the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better practice that all proceedings, even irregular ones, be set out in the record for inspection of reviewing authority. R. 26, 251, Dec., 1867.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate's duty to protect accused's rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge advocate's duty toward the accused is not confined to the limited province of 'counsel for the prisoner'; where the accused is ignorant and without counsel (especially an enlisted man) the judge advocate should ensure he does not suffer from ignorance of legal rights and has full opportunity to interpose pleas and defenses, including advising of right to plead statute of limitations and right to testify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to advise may not affect legal validity but may be ground for mitigation of sentence. R. 55, 182, Dec., 1887; C. 1885, Nov. 29, 1895; 16845, Oct. 3, 1904; 16974, Oct. 4, 1904; 18764, Feb. 8, 1907.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counseling accused to plead guilty generally inadvisable
rubrics_metrics.description: For the judge advocate to counsel the accused (when a soldier or inferior in rank) to plead guilty must, in general, be unbefitting and inadvisable; but where such plea is voluntarily and intelligently made, the judge advocate should advise of the right to offer explanatory or extenuating evidence and assist in securing it, and ensure opportunity to present a written or verbal statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate must prepare complete and accurate record
rubrics_metrics.description: It is one of the duties of the judge advocate to prepare the 'complete and accurate record' which every court-martial is required to keep; he should, if practicable, complete the record of each day's proceedings in time to be submitted to the court at the next session for approval or correction; the record is the record of the court and the judge advocate is subject to the court's direction in preparing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording judge advocate testimony when he is a witness
rubrics_metrics.description: If the judge advocate is required to give evidence as a witness, the clerk or reporter may record his testimony while on the stand; or, if there be no clerk or reporter, he may record his own testimony as that of any other witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of proceedings by judge advocate acting at close
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there have been two or more judge advocates successively detailed in the course of a trial, the one who is acting at the close is the one (and the only one) required to authenticate the proceedings by his signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record binding must be secure
rubrics_metrics.description: The method of holding together the leaves of a court-martial record by means of a clip is not sufficiently permanent to guarantee integrity; the method of binding is not prescribed but should securely fasten all leaves composing the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: External indorsement of the record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should be indorsed on the outside or cover so that the name of the accused, the court by which he was tried, with the time and place of trial, etc., will be apparent without opening and examining the proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing of records permitted with handwritten signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no legal objection to printing the record, or any part of it (such as orders, charges, and specifications), provided the signatures of the president and judge advocate are written by them in person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporter to be sworn by judge advocate and re-sworn per case
rubrics_metrics.description: In practice the reporter is sworn by the judge advocate; a form of oath is prescribed in the Manual for Courts-Martial. If the same party is employed as reporter for more than one case, he should properly be sworn anew in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate executes court orders
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the functions of the judge advocate of a court-martial is the execution of its orders; if a court adjourns subject to the call of the presiding officer, the judge advocate carries out the orders when notifying members of reassembly times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of dutiful performance by judge advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: The general presumption of law in favor of all public officers, in absence of affirmative evidence otherwise that they duly fulfill their functions, applies to the judge advocate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of judge advocate procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: An absence of the judge advocate from the court during the trial does not per se affect validity of the proceedings but should be avoided; court should suspend or adjourn for prolonged absence; no one can assume his duties except as court directs; record of meeting and adjournment in consequence of absence should be made as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate may be detailed to other duties if noninterfering
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate of a court-martial may be detailed to perform other duty (e.g., officer of the day or member of board of survey) if such duty will not interfere with his duties as judge advocate; but in general no duties in addition to those incidental to his function should be imposed pending an important trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff judge advocate cannot act as court judge advocate without detail
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer serving as judge advocate on the staff of a department or Army commander has as such no authority to act as judge advocate of a court-martial convened by such commander; he should be specially detailed for the purpose if desired to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation for retained civilian counsel limited and authorized only by Secretary
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no special provision of law for compensating attorneys retained as counsel to assist judge advocates; such counsel should not be retained except in important and complicated cases, and the authority of the Secretary of War for their employment should be sought and obtained; claims approved by judge advocate to be presented to Secretary of War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection as judge advocate evidences qualification; limits on employing civil counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of a certain officer as judge advocate is evidence that he is considered qualified to conduct prosecutions; employment of civil counsel to aid him can be authorized only by the Secretary of War or proper commander; to employ counsel without such authority or contract without sanction is irregular and unwarrantable and not binding upon the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: No official prosecutor other than judge advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than the judge advocate, military law recognizes no official prosecutor; the party who is the accuser or prosecuting witness may in important cases be permitted to remain in the courtroom and advise the judge advocate and may be accompanied by his own counsel; if such a party is to testify he should ordinarily be the first witness examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate's right to closing argument limited by evidence introduced
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge advocate is entitled to the closing argument or address to the court and may present an address even if the accused waives his right, but the judge advocate is not authorized to read to the court evidence or written statements not introduced upon the trial and which the accused has had no opportunity to controvert or comment upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmitting completed record to proper authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the court was convened by a military officer (e.g., general of the Army or department/Army commander) it is the duty of the judge advocate, upon completion of the record, to transmit the same to such officer (or successor) for proper action; where convened by the President, transmit directly to the Judge Advocate General to permit exercise of revisory function under section 1199, R.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate not subject to challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge advocate is not subject to challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate may challenge for cause (custom)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the custom of the service the judge advocate may also challenge for cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: No entitlement to trial by court-martial except by statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Except by authority of express statute, an accused can never be entitled to be tried by court-martial; where he is amenable to trial the Government may cause him to be tried or may waive a trial at its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifth Amendment principle as part of military common law
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution, though not the amendment itself, applies to courts-martial trials as part of common law military; an accused on trial before a court-martial cannot, when testifying in his own behalf, be compelled to incriminate himself as to an offense in respect to which he has not testified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of surgeons' records for identity evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: When an accused denies he is the person described in the charges, evidence of identity may be introduced which was secured by Army surgeons at time of physical examination required by Regulations and recorded in regular records, or secured by Army surgeons when the accused was a patient under their charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank of accused does not afford special defense privileges
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the accused is an officer of high rank should not be regarded as constituting a ground for allowing him any special right or privilege in his defense before a court-martial; administration of justice must be strictly impartial.
